newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S TELKOM SIGNS $170 MLN LOAN AGREEMENT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S TELKOM SIGNS $170 MLN LOAN AGREEMENT.

text.p: South African telecommunications parastatal Telkom on Monday signed a $170 million five-year term loan credit agreement with a syndicate of banks.
The loan was priced at 60 basis points above the London Interbank Offered Rate (Libor).
The syndicate, which was led by Credit Suisse and Sumitomo Bank Ltd, included banks from South Africa, Europe, the Far East and the U.S.
Credit rating agency Moody's had rated the loan Baa3 and Standard & Poor's rated it BB+ with a positive outlook.
The loan would be used to help fund Telkom's capital expenditure requirements as part of its Vision 2000 project, managing director Brian Clark said.
The project is aimed at adding three million new lines to its network and upgrading another one million lines to ensure a fully digital network by 2001.
